intent: Widen the sensor span from ±0.03 m to ±0.04 m (five sensors at 0.02 m spacing) so the outer sensors keep the 25 mm tape in view before the robot leaves it. All other geometry is held at the baseline, so the change in race result can be attributed to span. Expected result: line_loss_events drop from 1 to 2 toward 0 and max_error falls below the 0.06 m off-track limit, letting runs reach further progress on the oval and s-bend.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) The baseline's line losses come from the outer sensors being too close to the centre, so a ±0.04 m span should cut line_loss_events to near zero. (2) Max_error sits at the 0.06 m limit because the robot drifts past the sensor coverage, not because it oscillates, so the span fix should lower max_error. (3) Sensor lead y = 0.05 is not the cause of the drift, so steering_oscillation should stay below about 0.2 after the change. Measurements requested: per-track line_loss_events and max_error to see whether losses are concentrated on the slalom, and progress and completion_time to see whether the robot finishes. If oscillation rises, the sensor lead is the suspect; if rms_error is high with no losses, the sensor footprint is the suspect.
rationale: The baseline race (iteration 0, entityR2A) failed on all three development tracks. Every run ended off_track, with progress of only 0.11 to 0.16 and max_error near the 0.06 m off-track limit. Line-loss events were 1 to 2 per run, and steering_oscillation stayed low (0.14 to 0.17). So the robot drifts off the line rather than oscillating. The sensor span is the most likely geometric cause. The five sensors cover only x = ±0.03, and with the 25 mm tape the outer sensors lose the line once the lateral error passes about 0.02 m. The Integrator's feedback confirms the sensor span is the lever to try first. I therefore widen the span to ±0.04 m (five sensors at 0.02 m spacing), which keeps the tape under at least one sensor for larger offsets. I leave the sensor lead (y = 0.05), sensor_size (0.012), wheel_track, wheel_radius, body_width (the off-track limit is already at its 0.06 m floor, so widening the body does nothing), body_length and mass unchanged. This isolates one geometry change for the next race. Expected result: fewer line_loss_events and a lower max_error, with progress rising on the oval and s-bend. If oscillation rises instead, the next step is to reduce the sensor lead (y = 0.03). If rms_error stays high with no line loss, the next step is sensor_size 0.008.
